title: Medical emergency in Poland
question: How to call an ambulance and who gets free medical care in Poland?
short_answer: Call 112 (general emergency) or 999 (ambulance). Emergency care is provided to everyone regardless of insurance status. For non-emergency care you need NFZ insurance or pay privately.
conditions: Emergency care (pomoc doraźna) is FREE for everyone — including foreigners without insurance
With PESEL and NFZ insurance: most treatment is free
EU/EEA citizens: present EKUZ card for coverage equivalent to Polish residents
Non-EU without insurance: pay for non-emergency care, emergency is still free
24h duty pharmacy (apteka dyżurna): search at gis.gov.pl or ask any pharmacy
Night/weekend GP: Nocna i Świąteczna Opieka Zdrowotna — available at most hospitals
exceptions: Private insurance (Medicover, LuxMed, PZU Zdrowie): use their dedicated hotline for faster access
Dental emergency: covered in public hospitals even without NFZ
Psychiatric emergency: 116 123 (crisis line) or go to hospital SOR (emergency room)
